Right — the user said `export` goes on the declaration directly (e.g. `export double TriangleArea(...)`), not via `export namespace geo { ... }`. So `TriangleArea` is exported but not nested under a `geo` namespace. The `app.cpp` call uses `geo::TriangleArea`, so I need to either qualify with the module name or — more natural for the task — keep the namespace wrapping around the body. But the task explicitly forbids the `export namespace` wrapping block.

The cleanest solution: keep the `namespace geo` around the body for ADL/qualification purposes, and use `export` on the individual declaration. Re-reading the task:

> put `export` directly on TriangleArea's own declaration (not via a wrapping `export namespace { ... }` block)

So no `export namespace geo { ... }` block. But the task also says:

> Keep their bodies exactly as they are.

For `vec.cpp` the original body is `Vec2 Add(...)` inside `namespace geo { ... }`. If I remove the namespace and put `export` on each declaration, the unqualified `Vec2` types inside bodies still work (they're in the same module/declaration context), but `geo::TriangleArea` in `app.cpp` no longer resolves.

I need to keep `namespace geo { ... }` around the bodies (so `Vec2` is found and `geo::TriangleArea` still resolves) and add `export` to the individual declarations. The `export namespace` block vs. individual `export` declarations distinction is preserved — we're exporting `Vec2`, `Add`, `Cross` (and `TriangleArea`) individually, not via `export namespace geo`.
